content.title: About
content.content: Gluten‑free cookie is a baked treat made from gluten‑free flours (rice, corn, buckwheat, etc.) and often enriched with natural flavorings, nuts, dried fruit or chocolate. It is suitable for people with celiac disease and anyone following a gluten‑free diet.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gluten‑free cookies often contain more fiber than conventional ones because whole gluten‑free grains are used.
There are over 30 different gluten‑free flours, each giving the cookie a distinct taste and texture.
Many gluten‑free cookies are vegan when eggs and dairy are replaced with plant‑based alternatives.
Some brands use fermented starters to improve aroma and crumb structure in gluten‑free dough.
Gluten‑free cookies can have a longer shelf life since they lack the moisture that promotes mold growth.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Gluten‑free grains such as buckwheat and quinoa are high in dietary fiber, which promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: Certain gluten‑free flours (e.g., amaranth) raise blood sugar more slowly, which is beneficial for people with diabetes.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Gluten‑free grains often provide thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Cookies may contain magnesium, iron and zinc, essential for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Additions like dried fruit, nuts or cocoa boost antioxidant levels, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Gluten‑free cookies can contain nuts, soy protein or dairy, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Some varieties are sweetened with large amounts of sugar or syrups, increasing calorie load.

items.title: Additive presence
items.content: To improve texture, manufacturers may use additives such as xanthan gum, which some individuals prefer to avoid.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Even without gluten, cookies are often rich in fats and calories; moderation is key.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Gluten‑free cookies can be enjoyed as a snack, crumbled into yogurt, kefir, ice cream, or used in dessert recipes. They pair well with fruit sauces, nut butter or honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For extended freshness keep them in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation. Discard any cookies that show signs of mold or off‑odors.
